ai.description: This lizard reaches 45 cm in length. It is olive-brown with a dark nuchal crest and a prominent, black-bordered white patch on the throat. A distinct black stripe extends behind each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue for *Calotes nemoricola* is the presence of a distinct, black, crescent-shaped patch located just above the tympanum, which is absent in other species.
ai.habitat: The Nilgiri Forest Lizard inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests within the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal and typically hunts by remaining motionless on tree trunks, waiting to ambush passing insects with a rapid tongue strike.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes nemoricola* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–10 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between May and August in the Western Ghats.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nilgiri Forest Lizard is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily inhabiting the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka at mid-to-high elevations.
